data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims that genuine reasoning produces randomly distributed errors while mere checklist compliance produces structured errors clustering around checklist blind spots. This diagnostic criterion fails under the panel's own countercondition: a genuinely reasoning panel sharing a common bias (e.g., shared cultural background or training) would also produce structured, correlated errors. The target acknowledges this countercondition but provides no mechanism within a single evaluation to distinguish structured errors from shared bias versus structured errors from compliance. Since the claimed diagnostic (random vs. structured error patterns) cannot separate these two cases, it does not reliably distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance as the problem requires.
